candidate.title: RamDA-seq
candidate.scope: The RamDA-seq row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: single-cell poly(A) and non-poly(A) RNA is converted to amplified cDNA by RT-RamDA and then to a Tn5-prepared DNA sequencing library. The card title and complete middle row identify one target workflow; neighboring MATQ-seq and partially visible SINC-seq rows and the right-hand modified-nucleoside panel are separate poster content, not alternatives to this target. RT-RamDA is an embedded amplification component, not an additional target method. The primary paper (Hayashi et al., Nat Commun 9:619, 2018) clarifies this schematic; its C1 adaptation and advanced preparation settings are not additional extracted workflows. Sequential nicking and displacement pictures decompose a continuous RT amplification mechanism rather than specifying separate reaction incubations.

operations.label: Cell lysis
operations.description: Disrupts the single cell so that its poly(A) and non-poly(A) RNA become available as template for cDNA synthesis. The two RNA-class illustrations are not depicted as separately processed output fractions.
operations.information_effect: Releases the cellular RNA repertoire while retaining one-cell provenance through the individual workflow.

operations.label: 1st cDNA strand synthesis with RNase H minus RTase
operations.description: The depicted NSR primer addition enables synthesis of a complementary first DNA strand on the released RNA. The primary implementation uses oligo-dT together with NSRs (see correction c_primers); the schematic explicitly labels NSR only.
operations.mechanism: RNase H minus reverse transcriptase copies primed RNA into cDNA. NSRs are selected random hexamers designed to reduce rRNA-derived cDNA synthesis. This is preferential priming, not quantitative removal of rRNA from the input.
operations.information_effect: Encodes target RNA sequence in cDNA and admits non-poly(A) as well as poly(A) transcripts. Residual rRNA-derived DNA remains possible.

operations.label: Random nicks on cDNA by DNase I
operations.description: DNase I introduces random nicks into the cDNA strand of an RNA:cDNA hybrid, converting a newly synthesized hybrid into a nicked substrate for displacement amplification.
operations.mechanism: The primary figure specifies selective nicking of the DNA strand in the RNA:cDNA hybrid. This depicted role is distinct from an unshown upstream genomic-DNA digestion.
operations.information_effect: Creates internal sites from which reverse transcriptase can initiate displacement while RNA remains the template.

operations.label: Strand displacement amplification assisted by gp32
operations.description: Reverse transcriptase extends from the introduced nicks and displaces downstream cDNA, producing additional single-stranded cDNA products. T4 gene 32 protein (gp32) is an assisting binding protein, not another sample input or a separate output branch.
operations.mechanism: The strand displacement activity of RNase H minus reverse transcriptase is assisted by gp32; gp32 binds displaced single-stranded DNA and protects it from DNase I. The paper describes nicking and displacement as continuous events during RT.
operations.information_effect: Amplifies RNA-derived cDNA before second-strand synthesis. Random nicking/displacement in this implementation does not preserve a cell barcode or UMI for molecule counting.

operations.label: Tn5 transposase-mediated library prep
operations.description: Converts the double-stranded cDNA into the terminally marked DNA library shown at the end of the row. The paper identifies the broad block as Tn5 tagmentation-based Nextera XT library preparation; its routine internal steps are not separately expanded.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 tagmentation-based DNA library preparation, with the terminal marks interpreted as library-preparation handles rather than specified sequences.
operations.information_effect: The final DNA library supports sequencing-based measurement of represented poly(A) and non-poly(A) RNA, including coverage across transcript bodies and RNA-processing features as reported by the paper. Coverage does not guarantee recovery of every RNA. Read abundance is not UMI-resolved molecule counting, rRNA is incompletely suppressed, and this implementation does not provide strand-specific assignment of overlapping transcripts. A separate sequencing or analysis operation is not drawn.

method_scopes.rationale: All six local operations are connected within the row explicitly titled RamDA-seq, matching the assigned card. Poly(A) and non-poly(A) are target RNA classes entering one workflow, not alternative methods or separately sorted fractions. NSR primers, DNase I, gp32 and Klenow Fragment are reagents/components of this workflow. RT-RamDA names its embedded continuous first-strand amplification mechanism. MATQ-seq, SINC-seq and unrelated nucleoside structures lie in adjacent poster regions; no material-transfer arrows connect them to this row. The full-text paper establishes the RamDA-seq association and resolves the first-strand primer simplification and rRNA-selectivity overstatement.
